text:
maria: heads up — noticed a weird gap in eviction telemetry today that let a stale prefix stay hot after a handoff.

maria: we had a handoff to node-a at 09:11, but node-b kept serving the prefix for ~18s because it never saw the demote signal.

ben: yikes. did the handoff/lease ack skip the control plane or was it a race on the sequencer?

maria: looks like the sequencer accepted the new lease but the observer replica missed the demote because of a delayed delta stream. logs attached.

sam: can you paste the relevant log snippet? :thinking_face: 

maria:
```
[09:11:02] sequencer: lease-granted prefix=ten-x epoch=1234
[09:11:03] node-b: continue-serving prefix=ten-x last_seen_seq=98765
[09:11:20] node-a: start-serve prefix=ten-x epoch=1234
[09:11:21] node-b: eviction-suppress timeout expired, still serving
```

dana: is this the same as the "observer gap" we've discussed — where the demote/evict signal is not amplified to all serving threads?

maria: yep. node-b never recorded the demote event in its local prefix-state so its KV cache kept residency until local heuristics kicked in.

kevin: two quick ideas:
1) amplify eviction by writing a monotonic demote-counter to the control log so late/behind replicas can reconcile. (cheap: single int per prefix)
2) surface a telemetry check that asserts "last_handshake_epoch == last_demote_epoch" and fires an alert if mismatch > 5s

ben: both make sense. counter write solves eventual consistency but adds a small control-plane write. are we ok with extra writes on every handoff?

maria: handoffs are relatively infrequent compared to reads. tradeoff looks reasonable for correctness.

sam: what about piggybacking the demote lookups on normal read paths? e.g., when a read finds a prefix served locally, check control counter if last_seen_epoch < control_epoch and then trigger a fast local demote.

dana: piggyback reduces writes but adds a latency check on the read path — we must bound cost. maybe probabilistic: sample 1/100 reads for verification and also verify on lease acquisition.

ben: another angle — maintain a compact tombstone vector in the shared KV metadata that can be streamed via our delta channel; receivers apply tombstones idempotently. helps when delta stream is delayed but the vector is small.

kevin: agreed. Also want to add a per-prefix "observer-heartbeat" metric with tags {node, epoch, last_applied_seq}. We can then build an alert rule: if node claims serving but heartbeat shows stale seq for > Xs -> auto demote probe.

maria: Implementation sketch I wrote this morning:
```
on_handoff(prefix, new_epoch):
  control.write_demote_counter(prefix, new_epoch)
  sequencer.publish(prefix, new_epoch)

on_read(prefix):
  if local_epoch < control.read_epoch(prefix):
    fast_demote_local()
```

dana: sounds good. need to think about attack surface: what if control writes are delayed under partition — we should avoid making reads block on control reads.

sam: right. control.read_epoch(prefix) must be optional/async. fast_demote_local can be a best-effort background step that doesn't impede reads — it just marks cache as de-prioritized and eventually evicts.

ben: and add an idempotent apply path so reordering of demote counter and sequencer events cannot resurrect a prefix.

maria: for telemetry/alerting: propose two dashboards:
- per-prefix "demote-latency" histogram
- scatter of nodes where serve_count>0 but last_applied_epoch < active_epoch

kevin: add fallback policy: if mismatch persists > 30s, route reads for that prefix through the sequencer for verification (slow but safe) until resolved.

maria: ptal — I'll open an RFC PR with the counters + telemetry + fast-demote probe. anyone want to be co-author?

dana: I'll help with the telemetry/alerting bits.

ben: I can take the counter write + idempotent apply.

sam: I'll prototype the probabilistic read-sampling for verification.

maria: thanks all. filing thread as 1719999990 for tracking. will link RFC here when ready. :thumbsup:
